resources.string: Locks your vault now. You need your PIN to open it again.
Direct transfer: no waiting, with your PIN and password
Ask for a fingerprint, face or screen lock when opening VettID
Ask for the phone\'s PIN, pattern or password when opening VettID
Fingerprint or face; the phone\'s screen lock if they are not available
The phone\'s PIN, pattern or password only, never a fingerprint or face
Not available: this phone has no screen lock. Set a PIN, pattern or password in the phone\'s security settings first.
The app lock only keeps others out of VettID on this phone. It never replaces your vault PIN or credential password.
The app lock was turned off because a new fingerprint or face was added. Turn it on again if you like.
Your account name, display name and the items you tag @profile
Set by tag in your Vault. Nothing is shared without a rule.
Off. Screenshots, screen recording and the app preview in Recents are blocked.
On. Turns itself off when the vault locks, and after 1 hour.
On. A development build: it stays on until you turn it off.

Screenshots, screen recording and the app preview in Recents will show whatever is on screen, including messages and vault items. Anyone you show or send them to, and any app you let record the screen, sees the same.\n\nThis turns itself off when the vault locks, and after 1 hour. The screen for typing a recovery code stays protected.
Recommended. Most private: your phone keeps its own connection, and no Google or VettID push service is involved. Uses a little more battery.
Uses Google’s push service to wake VettID. Google learns only that VettID was woken, never who or what.
Needs Google Play services, which this phone does not have.
Google Play services need an update.
Not available in this build of VettID, which contains no Google software.
Not recommended. You see messages, requests, calls and security alarms only when you open VettID.
Your vault is locked: notifications resume after you unlock it
Notifications are blocked in Android settings
Battery optimisation may delay notifications until Android lets VettID use the network. Nothing is lost: VettID catches up when you open it.
Push unavailable, using the on-phone service
Google push is not available on this phone, using the on-phone service
Who it is from and what it is, never message text or item names
Also the message text and item names, never values or secrets
Sound, vibration and importance for each category, in Android settings
Notifications stay hidden on the lock screen until you unlock the phone, and are removed when your vault locks. Android’s Notification history, if you turn it on, keeps them outside VettID’s control.
Erase your vault and everything in it
Installed from: Google Play (signed by Google)
Installed from: F-Droid or direct (signed by VettID)

The Google Play version is signed by Google, so it trusts Google\'s signing; the F-Droid and direct versions are signed by VettID and do not. To change version, transfer your vault to the other version on another phone, or reinstall and recover it, which takes 24 hours.
Status comes from the account service and is for information only; your vault\'s own answers decide.
An update is available: release %1$d. Update it from Settings → Vault → Update available.
Your vault\'s release ends on %1$s. Update it before then (Settings → Vault → Update available), or the vault can no longer be opened.
Your vault\'s release has ended. The vault can no longer be opened.
Your vault\'s release has ended but is open for a rescue: unlock and approve the move to a current release.
Your vault\'s release is not available.
Your vault re-derives its key from the new PIN. Use at least 6 digits.
Choose a PIN different from the current one.

If you lose this phone, start a recovery on the account site. Your vault locks at once; after 24 hours the site shows a code that a new phone scans, and with your PIN and credential password the new phone takes over. This phone then erases VettID the next time it reaches your vault. While you still have this phone, use Move to a new phone instead: no waiting.

No recovery: your credential backup is off. If this phone is lost, broken, reset or replaced without a transfer, your vault cannot be recovered; it can only be deleted and replaced, and everything in it is lost.
State: %1$s. Available from %2$s. If you did not start it, cancel it now on the account site.
Your vault checks this phone\'s hardware key attestation at every enrollment and unlock, and this phone checks the vault\'s enclave against VettID\'s signed release list.

This erases your vault for good: your messages, connections, items, critical items and Protean Credential. Your connections are told the connection ended. It cannot be undone, and VettID cannot restore it.
Type the phrase exactly: delete my vault
I understand that my vault and everything in it will be erased and cannot be restored
This is the last step. Your vault is erased immediately.
Move VettID to a new phone: your credential moves there, and your vault and your connections then work with the new phone. This phone then erases VettID and keeps nothing of it.

1. On the new phone, install VettID, choose Move from my old phone and sign in to your account. 2. Show the code here and scan it with the new phone. 3. Check that both phones show the same 6 digits, then approve here with your vault PIN and credential password.
Lost your old phone instead? Start a recovery on the account site.
Scan this code with your new phone
On the new phone, choose Move from my old phone, then scan. Only your new phone should see this code.
Transfer code for your new phone
Or paste this code on the new phone
%1$s wants to take over your vault. Continue only if it shows the same code.
Nothing changes: your vault stays with this phone. The new phone is told it was rejected.
The new phone has another version of VettID
The new phone\'s VettID %1$s; this one %2$s. Continue only if you installed it yourself.
was installed from Google Play (signed by Google)
was installed from F-Droid or direct (signed by VettID)
is from Google Play (signed by Google)
is from F-Droid or direct (signed by VettID)
Your vault asked you to confirm the new phone\'s version of VettID first. Nothing was counted; enter your PIN and password again.
Your vault checks your PIN and your credential password, then moves your credential to %1$s. This phone then erases VettID and returns to the welcome screen, as if freshly installed.
This phone will no longer hold your credential or open your vault, and VettID erases everything it kept here. You cannot undo this from here.
Too many wrong tries. Try again in %1$s.
Nothing changed: your vault stays with this phone. Show a new code to try again.
Nothing changed: your vault stays with this phone.
Your vault works with %1$s now. This phone erases VettID as soon as your vault confirms the move; keep it online for a moment.
Another transfer is already open. It ends within 10 minutes; try again then.
Your credential has an open clone alarm. Resolve it in Credential before moving to a new phone.
VettID\'s published release list is used again. A vault on a release that is not published yet cannot be unlocked from this phone until VettID publishes it.
Your PIN was changed. Your vault\'s recovery now has 10 new attempts for the new PIN and your password.
Recovery attempts used: %1$d of 10. If that was not you, change your password now, and your PIN as well. That gives you 10 new attempts and ends the old ones.
All 10 recovery attempts were used. Recovery is off until you change your PIN or your password.
Recovery: set up at your next check.
Recovery: cannot be checked right now.
This vault\'s release does not offer recovery.

Finish the move on your new phone. This phone keeps your vault\'s keys until your new phone has finished the move, for at most 7 days. Before you give this phone away, remove VettID from it or reset it.
Recovery is off until you choose a new password that meets the rules.
If you fear that something ran as VettID on this phone
Your vault gives this phone a new secret. Your PIN stays the same, and the old secret opens nothing your vault stores from now on. Enter your PIN and your password.
If something ran as VettID on this phone, a new secret alone is not enough: move your vault to another phone, or recover it.
Your phone now uses a new secret for this vault.
Changing only the PIN gives whoever is guessing ten new tries at the same password. Change your password too.

For a day your vault has not been able to check its recovery attempts or record that you were here. If this goes on for three days, your vault is no longer protected against a recovery started by someone else, and until it ends you cannot change your PIN or password. This is a fault of the VettID service or an attack on it. Contact VettID.
